summary: ceil returns the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to its argument.
documentation: ceil returns the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to its argument. For Python floats its result is an integer, including when the input already represents a whole number.
inputs: A real number or an object implementing the ceiling protocol.
caution: For negative inputs, ceiling moves toward positive infinity. It is not truncation or rounding away from zero.
scenarios: Determine whole resource units for a positive estimate.
Convert a fractional page count into a required page count.
Apply an explicitly upward rounding rule to a planning estimate.
title: Round a planning value upward
problem: Input is a finite number. Return its mathematical ceiling as an integer. In particular, -2.7 becomes -2, not -3. Tests use exactly or unambiguously represented values.
goal: Use math.ceil() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
